text: The equations of two sides of a variable triangle are $x=0$ and $y=3$, and its third side is a tangent to the parabola $y^{2}=6x$. The locus of its circumcentre is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 25th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The parabola $y^{2}=6x$ has $4a=6$, so $a=\dfrac{3}{2}$ and the tangent at the point $\left (\dfrac{3t^{2}}{2},3t\right )$ is $ty=x+\dfrac{3}{2}t^{2}$.

The sides $x=0$ and $y=3$ are perpendicular, so the triangle is right-angled at $(0,3)$ and its circumcentre is the midpoint of the hypotenuse, which is the side on the tangent.

The tangent meets $x=0$ at $\left (0,\dfrac{3t}{2}\right )$ and $y=3$ at $\left (3t-\dfrac{3t^{2}}{2},3\right )$.


[IMG]

For the circumcentre $(h,k)$:

$2h=3t-\dfrac{3t^{2}}{2}\Rightarrow 4h=6t-3t^{2},2k=\dfrac{3t}{2}+3\Rightarrow t=\dfrac{4k-6}{3}$

Substituting $t$:

$4h=2(4k-6)-\dfrac{(4k-6)^{2}}{3}\Rightarrow 12h=24k-36-(16k^{2}-48k+36)$

$\Rightarrow 16k^{2}-72k+12h+72=0\Rightarrow 4k^{2}-18k+3h+18=0$

The locus is $4y^{2}-18y+3x+18=0$.

Hence, the correct option is (C).

sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 25th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\mathrm{L}:\frac{\mathrm{x}+1}{2}=\frac{y-1}{5}=\frac{z+1}{-1}=λ\text{(let)}$

Let foot of perpendicular is

$\begin{array}{l} \mathrm{P}(2λ-1,5λ+1,-λ-1) \\  \\ \mathrm{PA}\leftarrow =(3-2λ)\hat{\mathrm{i}}-(5λ+1)\hat{\mathrm{j}}+(6+λ)\hat{\mathrm{k}} \\  \\ \text{Direction ratio of line}\Rightarrow \vec{\mathrm{b}}=2\hat{\mathrm{i}}+5\hat{\mathrm{j}}-\hat{\mathrm{k}} \\  \\ \text{Now,}\Rightarrow \mathrm{PA}\leftarrow \cdot \vec{\mathrm{b}}=0 \\  \\ \Rightarrow 2(3-2λ)-5(5λ+1)-(6+λ)=0 \\  \\ \Rightarrow λ=\dfrac{-1}{6} \\  \\ \mathrm{P}(2λ-1,5λ+1,-λ-1)\equiv \mathrm{P}(α,β,γ) \\  \\ \Rightarrow α=2\left (-\dfrac{1}{6}\right )-1=-\dfrac{4}{3}\Rightarrow α=-\dfrac{4}{3} \\  \\ \Rightarrow β=5\left (-\dfrac{1}{6}\right )+1=\dfrac{1}{6}\Rightarrow β=\dfrac{1}{6} \\  \\ \Rightarrow γ=-λ-1=\dfrac{1}{6}-1\Rightarrow γ=-\dfrac{5}{6} \end{array}$

text:
The number of functions

$f:\{1,2,3,4\}\to \{a\in \mathrm{ℤ}:|a|\leq 8\}$

satisfying $f(n)+\frac{1}{n}f(n+1)=1,\forall n\in \{1,2,3\}$ is
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 25th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\because f:\{1,2,3,4\}\to \{a\in \mathrm{ℤ}:|a|\leq 8\}$

and $f(n)+\frac{1}{n}f(n+1)=1$

$\Rightarrow nf(n)+f(n+1)=n\ldots$ (i)

$\therefore f(1)+f(2)=1\Rightarrow f(2)=1-f(1)$

But $f(1)\in [-8,8]$

Hence, $f(2)\in [-8,8]\Rightarrow f(1)\in [-7,8]\ldots (\mathrm{A})$

and $2f(2)+f(3)=2\Rightarrow f(3)=2f(1)$

$\therefore 2f(1)\in [-8,8]\Rightarrow f(1)\in [-4,4]\ldots (\mathrm{B})$

and $3f(3)+f(4)=3\Rightarrow f(4)=3-6f(1)$

$\therefore f(1)\in \left [-\frac{5}{6},\frac{11}{6}\right ]...(C)$

From (A), (B) and (C) : $f(1)=0$ or 1

$\therefore$ Only two functions are possible.

sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 25th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

text:
Let A, B, C be 3 $\times$ 3 matrices such that A is symmetric and B and C are skew-symmetric. Consider the statements

(S1) A${}^{13}$ B${}^{26}$ $-$ B${}^{26}$ A${}^{13}$ is symmetric

(S2) A${}^{26}$ C${}^{13}$ $-$ C${}^{13}$ A${}^{26}$ is symmetric

Then,
options: Both S1 and S2 are false
Both S1 and S2 are true
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 25th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$A^{T}=A,B^{T}=-B,C^{T}=-C$

$\begin{array}{ll} P & =A^{13}B^{26}-B^{26}A^{13} \\  \\ P^{T} & =\left (A^{13}B^{26}-B^{26}A^{13}\right )^{T}=\left (A^{13}B^{26}\right )^{T}-\left (B^{26}A^{13}\right )^{T} \\  \\ =\left (B^{26}\right )^{T}\left (A^{13}\right )^{T}-\left (A^{13}\right )^{T}\left (B^{26}\right )^{T} \\  \\ =\left (B^{T}\right )^{26}\left (A^{T}\right )^{13}-\left (A^{T}\right )^{13}\left (B^{T}\right )^{26} \\  \\ =B^{26}A^{13}-A^{13}B^{26}=-\left (A^{13}B^{26}-B^{26}A^{13}\right )=-P \end{array}$

$P$ is skew-symmetric matrix $\Rightarrow S_{1}$ is false

$Q=A^{26}C^{13}-C^{13}A^{26},Q^{T}=\left (A^{26}C^{13}-C^{13}A^{26}\right )^{T}$

$Q^{T}=\left (A^{26}C^{13}\right )^{T}-\left (C^{13}A^{26}\right )^{T}=\left (C^{13}\right )^{T}\left (A^{26}\right )^{T}-\left (A^{26}\right )^{T}\left (C^{13}\right )^{T}$

$=\left (C^{T}\right )^{13}\left (A^{T}\right )^{26}-\left (A^{T}\right )^{26}\left (C^{T}\right )^{13}=-C^{13}A^{26}+A^{26}C^{13}$

$=A^{26}C^{13}-C^{13}A^{26}$

$\Rightarrow Q^{T}=Q\Rightarrow Q$ is symmetric matrix $\Rightarrow S_{2}$ is true.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 25th January Evening Shift

text: The shortest distance between the lines $x+1=2y=-12z$ and $x=y+2=6z-6$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 25th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Writing $x+1=2y=-12z=t$, the line $L_{1}$ passes through $(-1,0,0)$ with direction $\left (1,\frac{1}{2},-\frac{1}{12}\right )\| (12,6,-1)$.

Writing $x=y+2=6z-6=s$, the line $L_{2}$ passes through $(0,-2,1)$ with direction $\left (1,1,\frac{1}{6}\right )\| (6,6,1)$.

The common perpendicular is along

$(12,6,-1)\times (6,6,1)=(6+6,-6-12,72-36)=(12,-18,36)=6(2,-3,6)$

and $|(2,-3,6)|=\sqrt{4+9+36}=7$.

The vector joining the two points is $(0,-2,1)-(-1,0,0)=(1,-2,1)$, so

$\text{S.D.}=\frac{|(1,-2,1)\cdot (2,-3,6)|}{7}=\frac{|2+6+6|}{7}=\frac{14}{7}=2$

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 25th January Evening Shift

text: Let T and C respectively be the transverse and conjugate axes of the hyperbola $16x^{2}-y^{2}+64x+4y+44=0$. Then the area of the region above the parabola $x^{2}=y+4$, below the transverse axis T and on the right of the conjugate axis C is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 25th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$16x^{2}+64x-y^{2}+4y+44=0\Rightarrow 16(x+2)^{2}-(y-2)^{2}=16\Rightarrow \dfrac{(x+2)^{2}}{1}-\dfrac{(y-2)^{2}}{16}=1$

The centre is $(-2,2)$ and the transverse axis is parallel to the $x$-axis, so T: $y=2$ and C: $x=-2$.

The parabola is $y=x^{2}-4$; it meets $y=2$ where $x^{2}=6$, i.e. $x=\pm \sqrt{6}$. Since $-\sqrt{6}<-2$, the region to the right of $x=-2$ runs from $x=-2$ to $x=\sqrt{6}$, between $y=x^{2}-4$ below and $y=2$ above.


[IMG]

$A=\int\limits _{-2}^{\sqrt{6}}\left (2-(x^{2}-4)\right )dx=\left [6x-\dfrac{x^{3}}{3}\right ]_{-2}^{\sqrt{6}}$

$A=\left (6\sqrt{6}-2\sqrt{6}\right )-\left (-12+\dfrac{8}{3}\right )=4\sqrt{6}+\dfrac{28}{3}$

Hence, the correct option is (C).

text: Let the function $f(x)=2x^{3}+(2p-7)x^{2}+3(2p-9)x-6$ have a maxima for some value of $x<0$ and a minima for some value of $x>0$. Then, the set of all values of p is
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 25th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$f^{'}(x)=6x^{2}+2(2p-7)x+3(2p-9)$

A maximum at some $x<0$ and a minimum at some $x>0$ require $f^{'}(x)=0$ to have two real roots $x_{1}<0<x_{2}$. Since the leading coefficient of $f^{'}$ is positive, $f^{'}$ changes sign from $+$ to $-$ at $x_{1}$ (maximum) and from $-$ to $+$ at $x_{2}$ (minimum).

An upward-opening quadratic has its roots on opposite sides of $0$ exactly when its value at $0$ is negative; this also makes the discriminant positive, so the roots are real and distinct.

$f^{'}(0)=3(2p-9)<0\Rightarrow p<\dfrac{9}{2}$

So $p\in \left (-\infty ,\dfrac{9}{2}\right )$.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 25th January Evening Shift

text: Let $z$ be a complex number such that $\left |\frac{z-2i}{z+i}\right |=2,z\neq -i$. Then $z$ lies on the circle of radius 2 and centre :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 25th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\left |\frac{z-2i}{z+i}\right |=2$

$\Rightarrow (z-2i)(\bar{z}+2i)=4(z+i)(\bar{z}-i)$

$\Rightarrow z\bar{z}+2iz-2i\bar{z}+4=4(z\bar{z}-zi+\bar{z}i+1)$

$\Rightarrow 3z\bar{z}-6iz+6i\bar{z}=0$

$\Rightarrow z\bar{z}-2iz+2i\bar{z}=0$

$\therefore$ Centre $(-2i)$ or $(0,-2)$

Other Method :

$\left |\frac{z-2i}{z+i}\right |=2,z\neq -i$

Put $z=x+iy$

$\begin{array}{l} \left |\dfrac{x+iy-2i}{x+iy+i}\right |=2 \\  \\ \Rightarrow \left |\dfrac{x+i(y-2)}{x+i(y+1)}\right |^{2}=4 \\  \\ \Rightarrow x^{2}+(y-2)^{2}=4\left [x^{2}+(y+1)^{2}\right ] \\  \\ \Rightarrow x^{2}+y^{2}+4-4y=4\left [x^{2}+y^{2}+1+2y\right ] \end{array}$

$\Rightarrow$ $x^{2}+y^{2}+4y=0$ 

or $x^{2}+(y+2)^{2}=2^{2}$

$\therefore$ Centre is $(0,-2)$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 25th January Evening Shift

text: Let $f:\mathrm{ℝ}\to \mathrm{ℝ}$ be a function defined by $f(x)=\log _{\sqrt{m}}\{\sqrt{2}(\sin x-\cos x)+m-2\}$, for some $m$, such that the range of $f$ is [0, 2]. Then the value of $m$ is $_________$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 25th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Since $\sin x-\cos x=\sqrt{2}\sin \left (x-\dfrac{π}{4}\right )\in [-\sqrt{2},\sqrt{2}]$, the argument of the logarithm satisfies

$\sqrt{2}(\sin x-\cos x)+m-2\in [m-4,m]$

As $f$ is defined for every real $x$, the argument must stay positive, so $m-4>0$, i.e. $m>4$; then the base $\sqrt{m}>1$ and the logarithm is increasing.

So the range of $f$ is $\left [\log _{\sqrt{m}}(m-4),\log _{\sqrt{m}}m\right ]$, and the upper end $\log _{\sqrt{m}}m=2$ for every such $m$.

The lower end must be $0$: $\log _{\sqrt{m}}(m-4)=0\Rightarrow m-4=1\Rightarrow m=5$.

For $m=4$ the argument reaches $0$, where the logarithm is undefined, so the range cannot be $[0,2]$.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 25th January Evening Shift

text: Let $A=\left [\begin{array}{ll} \frac{1}{\sqrt{10}} & \frac{3}{\sqrt{10}} \\ \frac{-3}{\sqrt{10}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{10}} \end{array}\right ]$ and $B=\left [\begin{array}{ll} 1 & -i \\ 0 & 1 \end{array}\right ]$, where $i=\sqrt{-1}$. If $\mathrm{M}=\mathrm{A}^{\mathrm{T}}\mathrm{B}\mathrm{A}$, then the inverse of the matrix $\mathrm{AM}^{2023}\mathrm{A}^{\mathrm{T}}$ is
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 25th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{llllllll} \mathrm{AA}^{\mathrm{T}}=\left [\begin{array}{ll} \frac{1}{\sqrt{10}} & \frac{3}{\sqrt{10}} \\ \frac{-3}{\sqrt{10}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{10}} \end{array}\right ]\left [\begin{array}{ll} \frac{1}{\sqrt{10}} & \frac{-3}{\sqrt{10}} \\ \frac{3}{\sqrt{10}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{10}} \end{array}\right ]=\left [\begin{array}{ll} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \end{array}\right ]=I \\  \\  & \mathrm{B}^{2}=\left [\begin{array}{ll} 1 & -\mathrm{i} \\ 0 & 1 \end{array}\right ]\left [\begin{array}{ll} 1 & -\mathrm{i} \\ 0 & 1 \end{array}\right ]=\left [\begin{array}{ll} 1 & -2\mathrm{i} \\ 0 & 1 \end{array}\right ] \\  \\ \mathrm{B}^{3}=\left [\begin{array}{ll} 1 & -3\mathrm{i} \\ 0 & 1 \end{array}\right ] \end{array}$

Similarly, 

$\begin{array}{lll} \mathrm{B}^{2023}=\left [\begin{array}{ll} 1 & -2023\mathrm{i} \\ 0 & 1 \end{array}\right ] \\  \\ \mathrm{M}=\mathrm{A}^{\mathrm{T}}\mathrm{BA} \\  \\ \mathrm{M}^{2}=\mathrm{M}\cdot \mathrm{M}=\mathrm{A}^{\mathrm{T}}\mathrm{BA}\mathrm{A}^{\mathrm{T}}\mathrm{BA}=\mathrm{A}^{\mathrm{T}}\mathrm{B}^{2}\mathrm{A} \\  \\ \mathrm{M}^{3}=\mathrm{M}^{2}\cdot \mathrm{M}=\mathrm{A}^{\mathrm{T}}\mathrm{B}^{2}\mathrm{AA}^{\mathrm{T}}\mathrm{BA}=\mathrm{A}^{\mathrm{T}}\mathrm{B}^{3}\mathrm{A} \end{array}$

Similarly,

$\begin{array}{lll} \mathrm{M}^{2023}=\mathrm{A}^{\mathrm{T}}\mathrm{B}^{2023}\mathrm{A} \\  \\ \mathrm{AM}^{2023}\mathrm{A}^{\mathrm{T}}=\mathrm{AA}^{\mathrm{T}}\mathrm{B}^{2023}\mathrm{AA}^{\mathrm{T}}=\mathrm{I}.\mathrm{B}^{2023}.\mathrm{I}=\mathrm{B}^{2023} \\  \\ =\left [\begin{array}{ll} 1 & -2023\mathrm{i} \\ 0 & 1 \end{array}\right ] \end{array}$

$\therefore$ $\text{Inverse of}\left (\mathrm{AM}^{2023}\mathrm{A}^{\mathrm{T}}\right )\text{is}\left [\begin{array}{ll} 1 & 2023i \\ 0 & 1 \end{array}\right ]$

text: Let $f(x)=2x^{n}+λ,λ\in R,n\in N$, and $f(4)=133,f(5)=255$. Then the sum of all the positive integer divisors of $(f(3)-f(2))$ is
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 25th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$f(x)=2x^{n}+λ,λ\in \mathrm{ℝ},n\in \mathrm{ℕ}$

$f(4)=2\cdot 4^{n}+λ=133,f(5)=2\cdot 5^{n}+λ=255$

$\begin{array}{l} =\dfrac{8}{3}\ln 3-\dfrac{4}{3} \\  \\ =\dfrac{4}{3}(2\ln 3-\ln e) \\  \\ =\dfrac{4}{3}\ln \left (\dfrac{3^{2}}{e}\right ) \\  \\ m=4,n=3 \\  \\ m^{2}+n^{2}-5=20 \end{array}$

text: For the two positive numbers $a,b,$ if $a,b$ and $\frac{1}{18}$ are in a geometric progression, while $\frac{1}{a},10$ and $\frac{1}{b}$ are in an arithmetic progression, then $16a+12b$ is equal to $_________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 25th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body: $\begin{array}{l} \mathrm{a},\mathrm{b},\dfrac{1}{18}\to \mathrm{GP} \\  \\ \dfrac{\mathrm{a}}{18}=\mathrm{b}^{2}...(i) \\  \\ \dfrac{1}{\mathrm{a}},10,\dfrac{1}{\mathrm{b}}\to \mathrm{AP} \\  \\ \dfrac{1}{\mathrm{a}}+\dfrac{1}{\mathrm{b}}=20 \\  \\ \Rightarrow \mathrm{a}+\mathrm{b}=20\mathrm{ab},\text{from eq. (i)};\text{we get} \\  \\ \Rightarrow 18\mathrm{b}^{2}+\mathrm{b}=360\mathrm{b}^{3} \\  \\ \Rightarrow 360\mathrm{b}^{2}-18\mathrm{b}-1=0\{\because \mathrm{b}\neq 0\} \\  \\ \Rightarrow \mathrm{b}=\dfrac{18\pm \sqrt{324+1440}}{720} \\  \\ \Rightarrow b=\dfrac{18+\sqrt{1764}}{720}\{\because \mathrm{b}>0\} \\  \\ \Rightarrow b=\dfrac{1}{12} \\  \\ \Rightarrow \mathrm{a}=18\times \dfrac{1}{144}=\dfrac{1}{8} \\  \\ \text{Now},16\mathrm{a}+12\mathrm{b}=16\times \dfrac{1}{8}+12\times \dfrac{1}{12}=3 \end{array}$

text: Let $a\in \mathrm{ℝ}$ and let $α,β$ be the roots of the equation $x^{2}+60^{\frac{1}{4}}x+a=0$. If $α^{4}+β^{4}=-30$, then the product of all possible values of $a$ is $____________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 25th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$x^{2}+60^{\frac{1}{4}}x+a=0$

$\therefore α+β=-60^{\frac{1}{4}},αβ=a$

Now $α^{4}+β^{4}=-30$

$\Rightarrow \left (α^{2}+β^{2}\right )^{2}-2a^{2}=-30$

$\Rightarrow \left [(α+β)^{2}-2a\right ]^{2}-2a^{2}=-30$

$\Rightarrow \left (60^{\frac{1}{2}}-2a\right )^{2}-2a^{2}=-30$

$\Rightarrow 60+4a^{2}-4\cdot 60^{\frac{1}{2}}a-2a^{2}+30=0$

$\Rightarrow 2a^{2}-8\sqrt{15}a+90=0$

Product of value of $a=45$
